extracted.intended_audience: general public, fashion consumers, and readers interested in fashion/beauty news (including PR observers)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for crafting a corporate apology and response after an insensitive product or design causes public backlash, including removal, direct apologies, and commitments to prevent recurrence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Apology and removal of the offending item
rubrics_metrics.description: “We are deeply sorry for the distress caused by one of the products... Though the design was inspired by the marine theme... it was insensitive and we made a mistake.” and “we have removed it from the collection.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public response should include an explicit apology acknowledging distress, clear statement that the item has been removed from the collection, and an assurance that the company recognizes the mistake. Where appropriate, include a pledge to prevent recurrence (e.g., “I will make sure that this does not happen again”).

rubrics_metrics.name: Examine creative processes and increase diversity in decision-making
rubrics_metrics.description: The incident demonstrated the need for fashion houses to examine their creative processes and for “more diversity in the creative process.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brands should review internal approval workflows, ensure diverse perspectives are included in design and review stages, and create mechanisms for people with lived experience to inform creative choices. Position the brand as taking concrete steps to diversify voices and perspectives rather than only issuing statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid designs that evoke suicide or racially traumatic imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: Criticism that a look “resembling a noose” was insensitive — “Suicide is not fashion” — and that the shape evoked the “horrifying history of lynching.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Design and merchandising teams must be sensitive to mental-health implications and historical racial violence. Avoid motifs or styling that can reasonably be read as promoting or trivializing suicide or that recall racially violent symbols. When in doubt, seek external review from subject-matter experts or representatives of affected communities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respond to internal concerns promptly and respectfully
rubrics_metrics.description: Model Liz Kennedy said she asked to speak about the design but was told to “write a letter,” and that her concerns were dismissed; the CEO later called to apologize after becoming aware.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Establish and follow clear channels for employees/models/staff to raise ethical concerns; take reports seriously rather than dismissing them as 'it's fashion.' Follow up directly with affected individuals and, when appropriate, make direct personal apologies in addition to public statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintain professional conduct during production and show preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: Kennedy claimed staff were joking about the design before the show, while hanging the noose from a ceiling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enforce standards of professional behavior backstage and during preparation. Treat potentially sensitive elements with gravity; joking or casual treatment of potentially harmful imagery is an anti-pattern and can escalate reputational harm.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explain creative intent but do not excuse harm
rubrics_metrics.description: Designer Riccardo Tisci said the design was “inspired by a nautical theme” while also acknowledging “it was insensitive” and “it was never my intention to upset anyone.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When issuing explanations, state the creative intent transparently but avoid using intent as a blanket excuse. Combine explanation with acceptance of impact, apology, and concrete corrective actions to demonstrate accountability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include crisis resources when discussing suicide-related content
rubrics_metrics.description: The article provides a 'How to get help' section listing the National Suicide Prevention Lifeline and international crisis resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any reporting or public communication that references suicide or suicide-related imagery should include accessible crisis helpline information and resources for readers or affected individuals. This is both a public-health consideration and an editorial best practice.
